title: SHE SAID YES TO SCANDAL.
paragraphs: SHE SAID YES TO SCANDAL.

Not to applause.
Not to safety.
Not to a guaranteed explanation.
To scandal.
Nazareth was small. Tight streets. Tighter mouths. One whisper could stain a family for generations. And into that ordinary village life, heaven split the sky.
An angel stood before a teenage girl.
“Greetings, O favored one…” — Gospel of Luke 1:28
Favored?
Favor doesn’t usually look like this.
Because the message wasn’t comfort.
It was confrontation.
“You will conceive… and bear a Son… and you shall call His name Jesus.” (Luke 1:31)
And Mary knew exactly what that meant.

Unwed.
Unprotected.
Unbelieved.
In her world, pregnancy before marriage wasn’t gossip.

It was grounds for public shame. Even death under the Law (Deuteronomy 22:23–24). Some scholars interpret the severity of enforcement differently in first-century Judea—but the shame? The disgrace? That was real.
Feel the weight.

Joseph’s confusion.
Her parents’ silence.
The sideways glances at the well.
This wasn’t a Hallmark moment.
This was a cross before the Cross.
And yet…

Mary doesn’t argue reputation.
She doesn’t negotiate terms.
She doesn’t demand guarantees.
She asks one honest question: “How will this be, since I am a virgin?” (Luke 1:34)

Not unbelief.
Clarification.
When Gabriel answers that the Holy Spirit will overshadow her, that the child will be called the Son of God, heaven hangs on her reply.
And she says it.
“Behold, I am the servant of the Lord; let it be to me according to your word.” (Luke 1:38)
She said yes.

Yes to misunderstanding.
Yes to surrender.
Yes to carrying the promise before she saw the proof.
But don’t miss this—
Her “yes” didn’t save the world.
Her Son did.
Mary is blessed among women, but she is not the Savior. The Child in her womb is. The Gospel of Luke makes it clear: “For unto you is born… a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.” (Luke 2:11)
The scandal wasn’t the pregnancy.
The scandal was grace.

God stepping into human flesh.
Holiness wrapped in skin.
The Creator carried by His creation.
Why?
Because we said no.

No in Eden.
No in rebellion.
No in secret sin nobody sees but God.
We chose self.

So Jesus chose a manger.
Then a ministry.
Then a cross.

Mary’s “yes” opened the door.
Christ’s obedience closed the gap.
And here’s the fire in this story:
You may be one yes away from the will of God that terrifies you.

Yes to repentance.
Yes to confession.
Yes to surrendering that relationship, that addiction, that pride.

It might cost you reputation.
It might cost you comfort.
It will cost you control.
But on the other side of obedience?
Christ.

Grace greater than your scandal.
Purpose deeper than your fear.
Redemption stronger than your shame.
Mary carried Jesus in her body.
You carry Him by faith.
Today, heaven is still waiting for a yes.

Not to perfection.
To surrender.
Will you say it?
